about: American English: only the words an American kitchen says differently from copy/en.json, which is Australian (DECISIONS.md 55). A key missing here is copy/en.json's. Each entry's base is the English it was written against: test/copy.test.ts fails when copy/en.json moves and this does not, so a wording draft that changes one of these keys rewrites it here too. Design: LANGUAGE.md section 2.

action.hint.cold.base: eggs in the pan, lid on, then tap
action.hint.cold.text: eggs in the pot, lid on, then tap

controls.start.more.base: Boiling water: lower the eggs into water at a full boil. They peel more easily this way. Cold water: put the eggs in a cold pan, turn the heat on, and tap Full rolling boil when the water rolls. This is quicker overall. Sous-vide: I’ll tell you how long the eggs need in the water. It’s usually many hours, so plan ahead.

controls.water.more.base: How much water is in the pan, not counting the eggs. It matters most with the heat off, because then the hot water alone cooks the eggs. With the heat on it matters less. I also remember how long each amount takes to boil, so it’s worth measuring.
controls.water.more.text: How much water is in the pot, not counting the eggs. It matters most with the heat off, because then the hot water alone cooks the eggs. With the heat on it matters less. I also remember how long each amount takes to boil, so it’s worth measuring.

help.unsure.heatOff.base: With the heat off, I assume an ordinary pan with its lid on. A heavy pot or a loose lid will change the time.
help.unsure.heatOff.text: With the heat off, I assume an ordinary saucepan with its lid on. A heavy pot or a loose lid will change the time.

refusal.tap.base: A cold tap doesn’t cool the egg fast enough to stop the yolk cooking. Softest possible: {limit}. For a slightly softer yolk, use an ice bath.
refusal.tap.text: Cold running water doesn’t cool the egg fast enough to stop the yolk cooking. Softest possible: {limit}. For a slightly softer yolk, use an ice bath.

alarm.pull.bodyTap.base: Straight under the cold tap, or the yolk keeps cooking.
alarm.pull.bodyTap.text: Straight under cold running water, or the yolk keeps cooking.

refusal.counter.base: On the bench the yolk keeps cooking after the egg comes out. Softest possible: {limit}. For a softer yolk, cool the eggs in an ice bath.
refusal.counter.text: On the counter the yolk keeps cooking after the egg comes out. Softest possible: {limit}. For a softer yolk, cool the eggs in an ice bath.

controls.cooling.more.base: The yolk keeps cooking for a few minutes after the eggs come out of the water. An ice bath stops it fastest, so it allows the softest yolks, and a cold tap is nearly as good. On the bench the egg cools so slowly that the softest yolks aren’t possible, and the result varies more.

help.how.aside2.base: On the bench, still air takes heat out so slowly that the yolk ends up within a fraction of a degree of where it would if the egg never cooled at all. [README §5](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#5-carryover-the-cooling-step-is-part-of-the-recipe).

help.reliable.cooling.base: An ice bath gives the most reliable result, and a cold tap is nearly as good. On the bench the yolk keeps cooking, so use ice for soft eggs.
help.reliable.cooling.text: An ice bath gives the most reliable result, and cold running water is nearly as good. On the counter the yolk keeps cooking, so use ice for soft eggs.

help.unsure.counter.base: I’m least sure about cooling on the bench, because I couldn’t find any published measurements of how fast an egg cools in still air.
help.unsure.counter.text: I’m least sure about cooling on the counter, because I couldn’t find any published measurements of how fast an egg cools in still air.

controls.thermometer.more.base: When the cooling countdown ends, the middle of the yolk is at its hottest, and I’ll ask you for a reading. Push the tip right into the middle and tell me the highest number you see. Anywhere else, or any later, will read too low. The reading tells me how fast heat gets into your eggs. If you cool the eggs on the bench there’s no countdown, so I won’t ask.

advice.ice.base: Cool the eggs in an ice bath. On the bench it’s hard to say how much more the yolk will cook.

alarm.pull.bodyCounter.base: Out of the water and onto the bench.
